## Objective
- Extend the existing game with multiple hostiles, several guns, a fullscreen toggle, and an armory screen for weapon upgrades.

## Requirements
- Build a complete, playable game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Assumed “more players” means multiple AI impostors rather than online multiplayer.
- Added persistent credits and weapon ownership via `localStorage`; credits are earned from tasks and hostile takedowns.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated `index.html` with armory/fullscreen buttons, weapon HUD fields, and an armory modal.
- Partially updated `game.js` for four weapon options, three hostiles, credit rewards, armory rendering/purchase helpers, and fullscreen-related logic.

### Active
- Finish `game.js` event bindings and initial state; the attempted replacement of the existing handler block failed because the exact text did not match.
- Add CSS for the armory, HUD additions, and top action buttons.
- Check for remaining stale single-enemy references, run syntax/playability checks, and finish the game request.

### Blocked
- The final handler-block edit did not apply; no other blocking issue identified.

## Next Move
1. Read the current `game.js` lines around 56–57 and replace the handler block and initial `enemy` state with the planned armory, fullscreen, and multi-hostile setup.
2. Ensure the game loop pauses while the armory is open and that armory controls work both before and during play.
3. Add supporting styles in `style.css`, then test the game for runtime errors and playable progression.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: HUD and armory markup changes.
- `game.js`: gameplay and weapon system changes; currently unfinished.
- `style.css`: needs styles for new UI.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Current `game.js` still has its original handler block and initializes `enemy` at the bottom, despite other code now using `enemies`; finish this before testing.

- Complete the existing game with multiple hostile AI, several guns, fullscreen support, and an armory for weapon upgrades.

## Requirements
- Build a complete, playable game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

- “More players” was interpreted as multiple AI impostors, not online multiplayer.
- Credits and weapon ownership persist in `localStorage`; players earn credits from tasks and hostile takedowns.

- Updated `index.html` with armory and fullscreen controls, expanded weapon HUD, and armory modal.
- Updated `game.js` with four weapons, three hostiles, credit rewards, armory purchase/equip handling, fullscreen logic, and a paused game loop while the armory is open.
- Added CSS for armory cards, weapon options, credits display, and top action buttons.
- Fixed the initial enemy state to use `enemies`; added armory/fullscreen event bindings.

### Active
- Validate syntax, browser runtime, and playable progression; check for stale single-enemy references and UI issues.
- Finish with a brief note of the multiplayer assumption.

- (none)

1. Run `node --check game.js` and inspect the final changes for stale references or regressions.
2. Smoke-test starting, completing tasks, buying/equipping weapons, combat, defusing, fullscreen, and armory pause behavior.
3. Summarize the completed features and note that “more players” means AI hostiles.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: gameplay, enemy AI, weapon system, armory, and event handlers.
- `index.html`: game HUD, armory modal, and action buttons.
- `style.css`: styling for the HUD and new armory interface.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest event-binding and game-loop edits; rerun validation.
